findings.reason: the node cannot be built as written until it states where the third form is computed (the byte-identity test it already requires makes recomputation from the sliced prose possible) or drops the form.
findings.text: §16 states `_fingerprint_forms` "gains the present whole-document digest as a third recognised form" and that the predicate reads "the three `_fingerprint_forms` yields", but the same section deletes `_AuthoredProseParser` and says that form "is kept as the third recognised form by the sidecar census below rather than by recomputation", so the plan names no runtime producer for a value a pure function of the plan must return — a stored pre-change record cannot be recognised after the parser that computed its fingerprint is gone, which is exactly the re-review wave §14's correction (44 reviews) exists to prevent

findings.reason: the consolidation is one line naming `section_anchor` beside the delegation, and `evidence._section_key`'s free-text slugging branch genuinely differs, so the plan's current text is defensible as written.
findings.text: §16 rewrites `evidence._section_key` so "only its branch for identity-shaped input delegates to `section_record_id`" and keeps evidence's own empty→`_top` fallback, but `routing.section_anchor` already owns `section_record_id(section) or "_top"` and is imported by `promotion.py:76`, so the empty-identity fallback has two spellings the plan does not converge

rubric_items.deep_module: a finding — `_fingerprint_forms` is specified to yield three recognised digests but the plan deletes the only producer of the third and explicitly declines to recompute it.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding of low weight — the plan consolidates the `_top` empty-identity fallback inside `evidence._section_key` but does not name `routing.section_anchor`, which already owns exactly `section_record_id(section) or "_top"`.
rubric_items.interface_budget: pass — public_definitions 1478, cli_options 317, mcp_views 33, refusal_families 23; §16 and §17 each add only to `public_definitions` (three net, one and two respectively) and each states in its own text why nothing can be retired ("the identity digest and the prose walk keep their names"; "the two public readers ... are re-expressed rather than removed"), §16 reuses the existing `plan-review-missing` refusal family, and neither section adds a CLI option or MCP view.
rubric_items.reuse_search: pass — the plan cites the mechanism it extends for each new symbol, and every citation resolves in the tree: `strip_tags` reuses `_TAG_RE`/`count_open_decisions` (`reckon/_plan_html.py:1506`), the prose walk reuses `_PROSE_SKIP_TAGS` (`reckon/crew/plan_review.py:147`), the reader extends `_StructuredSectionSpanParser` (`reckon/_plan_html.py:44`), and the heading-walk census extends the module-private-rules pattern `_staged_writes` established (`reckon/interface_counts.py:97`).
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — the plan argues each new surface is a projection of one private read, not a parallel reader: `structured_section_spans` is "expressed as a projection of the parser's own span list rather than a second read", and the coverage predicate is stated to be "one function over those two existing readers, adds no walk of its own".
